title: Adjacency List Versus Adjacency Matrix for the Same Graph

guide.problem: Represent a network with clear edge meaning.
guide.design: Adjacency lists store neighbors; a matrix stores an entry for each possible pair. A matrix can be useful for dense graphs.
guide.invariant: Vertex indices are valid; edge direction and duplicate rules match the model.
guide.failure: Adding only one half of an intended undirected edge makes reachability asymmetric.
guide.trace: A directed edge 0->1 permits travel from 0 to 1, not automatically back.
guide.maintenance: Validate graph input before traversal and keep vertex identity separate from display labels.
